summary: This High-severity, already-Closed incident (classified BenignPositive/SuspiciousButExpected by the assigned analyst) fired on a rule that correlates a new local/domain account creation (4720) with that account being added to a privileged group (4732) within one hour, on host DC01.soclab.local. The only concrete telemetry provided is a single 4720 event at 2026-08-04T21:43:54Z showing the built-in SOCLAB\Administrator account (SID ...-500) creating an account named 'LabAttacker5'. No corresponding 4732 (privileged group addition) event is present anywhere in the supplied telemetry, so the 'rapidly elevated' half of the alert's own logic cannot be directly verified from the data given — it is only asserted by the alert/rule metadata. The surrounding host telemetry is dominated by routine Azure Monitor Agent extension update/reinstall activity and machine-account service logons, which is unrelated background noise. Separately, the host log window also contains a burst of NTLM authentication activity from external-looking IP 10.0.2.6 (an ANONYMOUS LOGON success and several 4625 failures against 'soclab.local\Administrator') roughly 20 minutes before the account creation; this activity is not evidenced as connected to LabAttacker5 or to the Administrator session that created it, but it occurred in the same log window and warrants separate scrutiny. The account name 'LabAttacker5' and the environment naming convention (soclab.local / rg-soc-lab) are strongly suggestive of an intentional lab/test or red-team account rather than a genuine adversary artifact, consistent with the prior analyst's BenignPositive call, but this cannot be confirmed purely from the telemetry — it is an inference from naming/environment context, not direct evidence of authorization.

attack_narrative.step: Baseline host telemetry begins; extensive Azure Monitor Agent extension install/update activity and machine-account (DC01$) service logons are observed on DC01.soclab.local — unrelated background/administrative noise.
SOCLAB\Administrator (SID ...-500) has an active Kerberos network logon session (EventID 4624, LogonType 3) on DC01.soclab.local.

A burst of NTLM authentication activity from external-looking IP 10.0.2.6 occurs: a successful NT AUTHORITY\ANONYMOUS LOGON (4624) and multiple failed logon attempts (4625) against 'soclab.local\Administrator'. No evidence links this activity to the LabAttacker5 account creation or to the Administrator session used to create it.

EventID 4720 recorded: SOCLAB\Administrator creates a new account named 'LabAttacker5' (SamAccountName=LabAttacker5, TargetSid ...-1106) on DC01.soclab.local. PrimaryGroupId is 513 (Domain Users) and UAC flags indicate a standard enabled account — no group-membership change is captured in this event.

Analytic rule 'New Account Created and Rapidly Elevated' fires (alert start/end time), asserting correlation of the above 4720 with a 4732 (privileged group addition) within one hour on the same host. No 4732 event for LabAttacker5 is present in the provided telemetry to substantiate this correlation directly.
Two duplicate SecurityAlert records are generated by Sentinel for the same underlying detection, both referencing the same 4720-based correlation.

Incident is closed by analyst rjrolander@yahoo.com with classification BenignPositive / reason 'SuspiciousButExpected', consistent with this appearing to be intentional lab/test account creation given the account name and lab-environment naming conventions (soclab.local, rg-soc-lab).

evidence: EventID 4720 at 2026-08-04T21:43:54Z, Computer=DC01.soclab.local, SubjectAccount=SOCLAB\Administrator, TargetAccount=SOCLAB\LabAttacker5, SamAccountName=LabAttacker5

Analytic rule description and alert MitreTechniques field (['T1136','T1098','T1136.001']) assert correlation of 4720 with a 4732 privileged-group-addition event within one hour, but no 4732 EventID for LabAttacker5 is present in the supplied SecurityEvent telemetry to directly confirm the group membership change occurred

recommended_actions: Query the Log Analytics workspace directly for the missing 4732 event (or 4728/4756 for domain groups) tied to TargetSid S-1-5-21-317907139-2069306354-2315969857-1106 (LabAttacker5) around 2026-08-04T21:44 to confirm whether the asserted privilege escalation actually occurred and which group it was added to.

Confirm with the lab/environment owner or change records whether 'LabAttacker5' was a planned test/red-team/purple-team account, since the account name and environment naming convention (soclab.local, rg-soc-lab) strongly suggest intentional lab activity but this is not independently confirmed in the telemetry.
Verify the current status of the LabAttacker5 account (enabled/disabled, group memberships, last logon) to ensure it was decommissioned after the exercise if it was indeed a test account.

Separately investigate the NT AUTHORITY\ANONYMOUS LOGON success and repeated failed NTLM logons against 'soclab.local\Administrator' from 10.0.2.6 around 21:22 UTC, as this pattern (anonymous session + failed admin logons) is independently suspicious and its relationship (if any) to the account-creation activity is unconfirmed.

Document the final analyst reasoning/evidence used to justify the prior BenignPositive closure (e.g., change ticket, exercise plan) for audit purposes, since the current evidence set alone does not fully substantiate authorization.
verification_needed: No 4732 (or equivalent 4728/4756) event for LabAttacker5 is present in the provided telemetry; the 'rapid elevation' half of the alert logic is asserted by the rule/alert metadata only and is not independently evidenced.

No process-creation (4688) or command-line evidence was captured showing exactly how/with what tool LabAttacker5 was created (e.g., net user, PowerShell New-LocalUser), limiting attribution of intent.

The relationship (if any) between the 21:22 UTC anonymous NTLM logon / failed Administrator logon attempts from 10.0.2.6 and the later LabAttacker5 account creation by Administrator is not established by the data — these could be unrelated, coincidental noise, or part of the same operator's activity.

No source IP, logon type, or session details are attached directly to the 4720 event itself, so it cannot be confirmed whether the account was created interactively at the console, via RDP, or via a remote/scripted mechanism.

Confirmation of whether this is a designated, pre-authorized lab/test environment activity (vs. genuine compromise) relies on naming-convention inference only and has not been corroborated with a change ticket, exercise plan, or owner statement in the evidence provided.
